title: Derived-unit resolution calculation in a proper/open tower
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Let $X,U,\overline X,Y,\overline Y,Z$ be Noetherian schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Suppose that $j:X\hookrightarrow U$, $b:U\hookrightarrow\overline X$, and $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], that $q:U\to Y$, $p:\overline X\to\overline Y$, and $s:\overline Y\to Z$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and that $pb=iq$. Put $a=bj$. On small etale sites use constant-$A$ module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; $Dk_!$ denotes exact termwise open extension and $Rt_*$ total derived direct image as in [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Write $\chi:i_!q_*\xrightarrow{\sim}p_*b_!$ for the section-preserving proper-support identification [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition], and $\Gamma_Q:Di_!Rq_*\to Rp_*Db_!$ for the specified proper/open comparison [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange].

For any K-injective complex $J$ on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], choose K-injective resolutions $u:j_!J\to I$ on $U$, $v:b_!I\to M$ on $\overline X$, and $w:i_!q_*I\to L$ on $\overline Y$. Then $q_*I$ and $p_*M$ are K-injective, and there is a chain map $\ell:L\to p_*M$, unique up to homotopy subject to
$$\ell w\simeq (p_*v)\chi_I.$$
The following two maps, with source $s_*i_!q_*j_!J$ and target $s_*p_*M$, are chain homotopic:
$$ (s_*\ell)(s_*w)(s_*i_!q_*u)
\quad\text{and}\quad
(s_*p_*(v\circ b_!u))\,(s_*\chi_{j_!J}). $$
Moreover $v\circ b_!u:a_!J=b_!j_!J\to M$ is a K-injective resolution. With the canonical open-extension and derived-direct-image composition identifications [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], the first path represents the successive derived-functor unit maps for $q_*$ and $s_*$, followed by $Rs_*\Gamma_Q$ and these composition identifications, whereas the second path represents the single derived-functor unit for $(sp)_*$ applied to $a_!J$, after the section-preserving sheaf identification $s_*i_!q_*j_!=s_*p_*a_!$. These identifications are natural in maps of K-injective representatives and independent of the chosen resolutions $I,M,L$, as maps from the specified localized termwise source. No exactness of $q_*j_!$, $s_*i_!$ or $(sp)_*a_!$ is assumed; the units here are maps from localized termwise complexes.

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), explicit K-injective comparison; Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), proper/open tower calculation; sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), resolution normalization. The equality of the two unit paths is the extracted chain-level argument.

proof.text: For each of $q,p,s$, the constant-$A$ inverse image is an exact additive left adjoint to direct image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies to these module categories. It gives K-injectivity of $q_*I$, $p_*M$, $s_*L$, and $s_*p_*M$. No properness or exactness of direct image is used in this application; the needed exact functor is inverse image. All the termwise functors in the calculation are additive and therefore preserve chain homotopies: applying an additive functor to $f-g=dh+hd$ gives the same equation with its image of $h$.

The open-extension composition isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] identifies $a_!J$ with $b_!j_!J$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], $b_!u$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $t:=v\circ b_!u:a_!J\to M$ is a quasi-isomorphism as a composite of two such maps. Its target is K-injective by the choice of $M$, so it is a K-injective resolution by [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions].

source.place: Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open), resolution construction; horizontal composition calculation (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal); exactness: sites-modules.tex Tag 03DJ

proof.text: Put $B=i_!q_*I$ and $c=(p_*v)\chi_I:B\to p_*M$. In the derived category $Qw:QB\to QL$ is invertible, since $w$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], with K-injective target $p_*M$ from step 1, represents $Qc\circ(Qw)^{-1}$ by a chain map $\ell:L\to p_*M$, unique up to homotopy. The same bijection with source $B$ shows $\ell w\simeq c$. Conversely this equation determines $Q\ell=Qc\circ(Qw)^{-1}$, hence determines its homotopy class. Here and below $Q$ means the localization at quasi-isomorphisms specified by [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

Naturality of the section-preserving sheaf identification [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition], applied degreewise to $u:j_!J\to I$, gives $\chi_I(i_!q_*u)=(p_*b_!u)\chi_{j_!J}$. Choose a homotopy $h$ with $\ell w-c=dh+hd$ from step 3. Applying $s_*$ and precomposing with the chain map $s_*i_!q_*u$ gives a homotopy $s_*h\circ s_*i_!q_*u$ between the first displayed path and $s_*c\circ s_*i_!q_*u$. Substitute the naturality equation and use functoriality of $p_*,s_*$ to obtain exactly $s_*p_*(v\circ b_!u)\circ s_*\chi_{j_!J}$, the second path. Additivity of $s_*$ is included in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

proof.text: Use the existing Functor.rightDerivedFunctorUnit and rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso. For any map h:K→M with K-injective M, naturality of the unit, followed by its inverse at M, proves η_K;R(Qh);η_M⁻¹=Q(t_*h). This is proved explicitly in each of the two formula modules, without any exactness assumption on direct image.

proof.text: Apply step 5 first to $q_*$ and $u$, then to $s_*$ and $w$. After termwise $i_!$ and $s_*$, the two resolution maps are $s_*i_!q_*u$ and $s_*w$, respectively. The representative formula in [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange], applied to the square with top edge $b$, bottom edge $i$, and K-injective input $I$, says that $\Gamma_{Q,QI}$ is represented by $c=(p_*v)\chi_I$. Under the resolution $w:B\to L$ this is represented by $\ell$, because $\ell w\simeq c$. Both $L$ and $p_*M$ are K-injective, so the action of $Rs_*$ on that morphism is represented by $s_*\ell$ by [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Consequently the successive units followed by $Rs_*\Gamma_Q$ are represented by the first displayed path. The square here need not be cartesian; the cited comparison explicitly allows a commutative proper/open square. In Lean this calculation is proved as [lem-sfb-proper-open-tower-successive-unit-formula]; its proof uses the generic unit and canonical composition API directly.

Apply the unit naturality identity of step 5 to (p then s)_* and the total augmentation of step 2. Expand the canonical open-composition comparison and cancel its inverse. Naturality of the underived direct-image composition moves the augmentation to M, where the forward and inverse comparison cancel. This is exactly [lem-sfb-proper-open-tower-single-unit-formula], proved using the existing total-right-derived unit API and the open-composition isomorphism [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. The section-preserving comparison from [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition] is precomposed unchanged. The successive formula uses the generic canonical composition API, as proved in [lem-sfb-proper-open-tower-successive-unit-formula], so no ringed-topos composition theorem is needed.

proof.text: For a chain map $f:J\to J'$ of K-injective representatives and resolutions $u',v',w'$ for $J'$, use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to choose maps $\alpha:I\to I'$, $\beta:M\to M'$, $\gamma:L\to L'$ satisfying, in the homotopy categories, $\alpha u=u'j_!f$, $\beta v=v'b_!\alpha$, and $\gamma w=w'i_!q_*\alpha$. For example $Q\alpha=Q(u'j_!f)(Qu)^{-1}$; the other two are obtained by the same displayed formula with $(v,v'b_!\alpha)$ and $(w,w'i_!q_*\alpha)$. Each target $I',M',L'$ is K-injective by choice, so the cited bijection supplies the map and uniqueness of its homotopy class. These are applications of the Hom bijection, not assertions of degreewise lifting through a monomorphism.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), derived morphisms into K-injectives and cancellation of quasi-isomorphisms

proof.text:
Write $\ell'$ for the primed comparison. Using step 8 and naturality of $\chi$ from [lem-cbc-proper-support-sheaf-composition], calculate in the homotopy category
$$p_*\beta\,\ell w=p_*\beta\,p_*v\,\chi_I=p_*v'\,p_*b_!\alpha\,\chi_I=p_*v'\,\chi_{I'}\,i_!q_*\alpha=\ell'\gamma w.$$
The target $p_*M'$ is K-injective by step 1. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], cancellation of the invertible $Qw$ implies $p_*\beta\,\ell\simeq\ell'\gamma$. Apply $s_*$ and precompose with the augmented source maps: step 8 now gives commutativity of the first-path naturality square with source map $s_*i_!q_*j_!f$ and target map $s_*p_*\beta$. For the second path, $\beta t=t'a_!f$ in the homotopy category follows directly from the two equations for $\alpha,\beta$; naturality of $\chi$ gives the identical square. Thus the identifications of steps 6 and 7 are natural in $f$.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective); explicit naturality calculation for more-etale.tex Tag 0F7B

proof.text: For two choices of $I,M,L$ at fixed $J$, apply steps 8 and 9 to $f=\mathrm{id}_J$. The equation $\alpha u=u'$ implies $Q\alpha$ is invertible. Exactness of $b_!$ [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] then implies $Q\beta$ is invertible from $\beta v=v'b_!\alpha$. The map $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives, hence a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; its images under $q_*$ and $i_!$ are homotopy equivalences. The equation for $\gamma$ therefore makes $Q\gamma$ invertible too. Thus $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ are homotopy equivalences, and so is $s_*p_*\beta$. Their homotopy classes over the augmentations are unique by step 8, and comparison maps for three choices compose to the unique such maps. Step 9 identifies the two delivered morphisms under these canonical target comparisons, with the source fixed as $Q(s_*i_!q_*j_!J)$. If $J$ itself is replaced by a quasi-isomorphic K-injective representative, its comparison is a homotopy equivalence by the same cited result and the termwise source comparison is likewise invertible. This is the claimed independence on K-injective representatives and resolutions; it makes no assertion that the termwise source functor descends on arbitrary complexes.
